# Prabhu Natarajan — UX/UI Designer

> UX/UI designer and HFI Certified Usability Architect (CUA)™ in Chennai, India. Designing for the web since 2005; Assistant Manager, UX/UI at Samsung’s Digital e-Commerce Division from 2016 to 2026. Available for full-time UX/UI roles and freelance projects.

- Website: https://www.prabhunatarajan.com/
- Email: me@prabhunatarajan.com
- Location: Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India (IST, UTC+5:30); works with teams in the US, the Gulf, Europe and Asia
- Résumé (PDF): https://www.prabhunatarajan.com/assets/Prabhu-Natarajan-UX-UI-Designer-Resume.pdf

## Selected work

- **Nebuloan** (Mortgage fintech, web app): A dark-mode workspace for mortgage teams. The loan pipeline, a single-loan view that puts the property, borrower and credit details side by side, and a data-flow view that surfaces exceptions before they stall a file.
- **SBA disaster loan application** (Government lending, multi-step form): An application wizard for the U.S. Small Business Administration’s COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loan program. Business and owner details, eligibility disclosures, bank linking through Plaid, document upload, review and e-sign — with progress visible at every step, so small-business owners always know how far they have left.
- **Emirates Raffle** (Sustainability eCommerce, responsive site): A UAE raffle platform where ticket sales fund eco parks, carbon offsets and food security. I designed and built the whole site: light and dark themes, live-countdown raffle cards, community showcases and a mobile-first path from browsing to buying a ticket.
- **Lykas** (Personal finance, landing page): A personal-finance landing page that makes financial advice feel approachable. Friendly illustration, a clear summary of what members get, and goal-based entry points — cash flow, taxes, education, real estate, retirement — so visitors start from what they care about.
- **Samsung.com/us checkout and My Account** (eCommerce, 2016–2026): Ten years in Samsung’s Digital e-Commerce division on the screens that turn browsing into orders: cart, payment and confirmation, plus My Account. Responsive, localised for several countries including Arabic right-to-left, and backed by 250+ transactional email templates for orders, exchanges and offers.
- **Self-ordering kiosk for food courts** (B2B self-ordering kiosk, food courts): A self-ordering platform that restaurant brands buy for their food courts. I redesigned the whole flow, from items and add-ons to paying by card or UPI. The receipt printer sits well below eye level, and the first success screen showed only an arrow, so people walked off without their receipt. Now the screen shows the receipt printing, with an arrow leading down to the slot, and people pick it up straight away. Case study: https://www.prabhunatarajan.com/work/food-court-kiosk.html

## How he works

1. Understand: user interviews, personas, journey maps and a heuristic review of what exists today.
2. Structure: information architecture, task flows and wireframes, tested with users before polish.
3. Design: high-fidelity UI, prototypes, micro-interactions and design systems.
4. Ship: accessible, semantic front-end code or developer-ready specs, then design QA.

## Common questions

### Who is Prabhu Natarajan?

Prabhu Natarajan is a UX/UI designer and HFI Certified Usability Architect (CUA)™ based in Chennai, India. He has designed for the web since 2005, most recently as Assistant Manager, UX/UI in Samsung’s Digital e-Commerce Division from 2016 to 2026.

### Is Prabhu available for new work?

Yes. He’s available for full-time UX/UI roles and freelance projects. The quickest way to reach him is by email at me@prabhunatarajan.com.

### What does Prabhu do as a UX/UI designer?

He works across the whole process: user research, personas, journey mapping and heuristic reviews, then information architecture, wireframes and prototypes, then high-fidelity UI and design systems, and finally accessible front-end code or developer-ready specs with design QA.

### Which industries has he designed for?

eCommerce, fintech, mortgage, healthcare, real estate, edtech and government lending. His work includes Samsung.com/us checkout, the Nebuloan mortgage workspace and the SBA COVID-19 disaster loan application.

### Does Prabhu write front-end code?

Yes. He writes semantic, accessible HTML, CSS/SCSS and JavaScript, builds WCAG-compliant interfaces, and can work in Angular, React or Vue codebases when the build drifts from the design.

### Can he work with teams outside India?

Yes. He works from Chennai on Indian Standard Time (UTC+5:30) and has designed with teams in the US, the Gulf, Europe and Asia.

### What freelance work does Prabhu take on?

UX audits and usability reviews of an existing product, redesigns of key flows such as sign-up, checkout and long forms, design systems, and accessible, WCAG-compliant front-end builds. He can take on one part of a product or the whole journey, from research to shipped UI.

### How does a freelance project with Prabhu start?

Email me@prabhunatarajan.com with a few lines about the product, who uses it, what isn’t working and when you need it. That’s enough for a first conversation about scope and approach.

### What does a client get at the end of a project?

Whatever your team needs to build from: Figma designs and prototypes with developer-ready specs, or production-ready HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Accessibility is designed in from the start, not added at the end.
